content.title: WEIRD SIGNS YOUR BODY IS SILENTLY MISSING A KEY NUTRIENT
facts: **Cracked, red corners of your mouth** – a classic sign of low **riboflavin (B2)** or **iron**, not just dry weather.
**Restless legs at night** – that crawling, twitchy urge to move your legs is often linked to low **iron** or **magnesium** stores, even without anemia.
**White spots on your nails** – frequently blamed on calcium, but more often tied to a **zinc** shortfall.
**Night blindness** – struggling to adjust when lights go out can point to low **vitamin A**, which your retina depends on to process dim light.
**Bleeding, swollen gums** – not always a brushing problem; it can signal low **vitamin C**, needed to keep gum tissue and blood vessels strong.
**Numb or tingling hands** – beyond B12, this can also show up with low **vitamin E**, which protects nerve membranes from damage.
**Brittle hair that snaps easily** – often traced back to low **biotin** or **protein**, not just harsh shampoo.
**Muscle cramps that hit out of nowhere** – classic sign your **potassium** or **magnesium** levels have dipped.
**Slow-healing cuts and scrapes** – your skin needs **vitamin C** and **zinc** to rebuild collagen and close wounds efficiently.

caption:
A few of these signs deserve extra attention. Cracked corners of your mouth aren't just from cold weather — low riboflavin or iron disrupts how your skin cells regenerate, so tiny cracks stop healing normally. Restless legs at night is another sneaky one: iron plays a direct role in dopamine production, and when levels drop, that nerve signaling gets glitchy, leading to that itchy, must-move feeling right when you're trying to sleep. And those white spots on your nails? Zinc is essential for the protein that builds your nail bed, so even a mild dip can show up as visible marks weeks later. Everyone's body is different, so treat these as clues to look into, not a diagnosis.
